parameters.note: Daggett Creek is an intermittent east-slope creek in the Carson Range that flows EAST — from just below Daggett Pass (Kingsbury Grade, NV 207) down toward the Carson Valley floor in Douglas County, Nevada. Daggett Pass is the drainage divide 'on the border between the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit to the west and the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest to the east' (Wikipedia), so Daggett Creek drains to the Carson River watershed (Carson Valley), NOT to Lake Tahoe. It is therefore NOT covered by NDOW's Douglas County 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing (which is restricted to Tahoe-basin waters and imposes 1-hour-before-sunrise-to-2-hours-after-sunset hours). Daggett Creek is not named in the Douglas County CLOSED WATERS list (Topaz Marina jetties, the Cave Rock boat-launch area, and Glenbrook Creek from Lake Tahoe to Highway 50), so it falls under the Douglas County OPEN WATERS general regulation: 'All waters (Except as noted below) — Open year around', with the county's general limits and any-hour fishing. Because the creek is intermittent, its fishery is limited; no source names any fish species or stocking for it, so species and stocking are left empty.

candidates.summary: Open year-round under the Douglas County general open-waters regulation. Daggett Creek drains east of Daggett Pass to the Carson Valley (Carson River watershed) and is NOT a Lake Tahoe tributary, so the 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing does not apply; it is also not among the county's closed waters.

parameters.counting_rule: Douglas County general open-waters limit: daily 5 trout, 5 mountain whitefish, and 15 warmwater game fish (of which not more than 5 may be black bass and 5 may be walleye); possession 10 trout, 10 mountain whitefish, and 30 warmwater game fish (of which not more than 10 may be black bass and 10 may be walleye). The 5/10 shown here is the trout component of that combined structure.

candidates.summary: Douglas County general limits: 5 trout, 5 mountain whitefish, and 15 warmwater game fish daily (max 5 black bass, 5 walleye); possession 10 trout, 10 mountain whitefish, 30 warmwater game fish (max 10 black bass, 10 walleye).

candidates.citation: NV CR 25-16 (Douglas Co. — OPEN WATERS: All waters)

parameters.note: The Douglas County general open-waters regulation allows fishing 'Any hour of the day or night' — unlike the county's 'Lake Tahoe and tributaries' listing, which restricts hours to 1 hour before sunrise through 2 hours after sunset. Daggett Creek, being an east-slope Carson Valley water rather than a Tahoe tributary, follows the any-hour general rule.

candidates.summary: Fishing allowed any hour of the day or night (Douglas County general open-waters rule; no time-of-day restriction).

parameters.note: Nevada requires a fishing license for residents and nonresidents 12 years of age or older; anglers under 12 need no license (nonresidents under 12 are limited to 50% of the daily bag). Daggett Creek is a Carson Valley drainage water, not part of Lake Tahoe, so no Lake Tahoe California/Nevada license reciprocity applies — a Nevada fishing license is required.

candidates.summary: Nevada fishing license required for anglers 12+.
